$schema_note: Deterministic structure of a NEW-SYSTEM (data-mx) Season Review special. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the format's structure — consumed by validate-chapter-plan.py (mx-special checks, WP-6) and scripts/stitch_specials.py (skeleton-driven assembly). The plan selects/repeats slots via each chapter's `skeleton_slot`; ALL chrome (masthead, cover, act openers, transit seams, chapter plates, footer) is stitcher-owned and unrepresentable in writer files. Spec: docs/design-system-unification-SPEC-2026-07-18.md Part 1 (Laws 2/3/5/6/7), Part 7 §2-§4, WP-6.

law2.planned_density_note: Plan-time reachability check (validate-chapter-plan.py): est_screens_390 = words/250 + 0.5 x total_planned_events (calibrated against the WP-1/WP-2 measured packs: countdown 6,380w/115ev -> 82.7 est vs 80.2 measured; DD re-dress 18,429w/84ev -> 115.7 est vs 115.5 measured). total_planned_events = sum(chapters[].visual_events) + structural events the stitcher emits (one plate per chapter + one act opener per act + one transit per act seam). Reject when total/est_screens < law2.floor. The rendered publish-gate (tools/measure-issue.mjs) stays the ground truth; this check only rejects plans that cannot possibly reach the floor.

acts.note: issue_meta.acts declares 2-3 acts: [{name, title, hand, grounds[], tokens?{}, transit_card?}]. grounds are core scene-ground utilities (>=1 per act, Law 1). Act palettes come from a motif pack (preferred; e.g. references/motif-packs/matchday-worldcup.json) or per-act `tokens` maps; the stitcher refuses a flat act (no pack AND no tokens).

timing.note: Part 7 §2 — a Season Review REQUIRES the season/tournament CONCLUDED strictly before publish date. issue_meta.event = {name, start_date?, end_date, status:'concluded'}. end_date < issue_meta.date, strictly: attempt #2 scheduled a Season Review the morning BEFORE the final (end_date == publish date) — that plan must be impossible.

signature_moment.note: Law 5: Season Review's signature — leaderboard/scorecard rows climb into place. The stitcher stamps the class on the chapter wrapper whose skeleton_slot matches; mx-motion.js sequences tr/li/.mx-ranked__entry children under tier1/tier2.

cover.gesture: bracket/trophy motif — oversized season-code ghost (e.g. 25/26) behind a poster cover; pack cover_plate art consumed into .mx-cover__plate when the motif pack ships one

chrome.note: Stitcher-owned, writer-unrepresentable: one .mx-mast, poster cover, .mx-actopen per act, .mx-transit per act seam, one .mx-plate per chapter (auto-numbered), back pill, .mx-footer colophon. Structural events counted at plan time: plates = n_chapters, act openers = n_acts, transits = n_acts - 1.

slots.notes: The season's shape in one screenful: stat band + facts ledger before any narrative.
The champion's arc — the season's spine, anchored on a figure block and at least one named voice.
Turning points as kit objects (clipping cards / tickets), each tied to a date. Awards later must point back at these.
Optional narrative chapters: chasing pack, relegation, managers, europe.

THE KILLER FEATURE (Part 7 §3): 8-12 per-club/team scorecards, each a matchday/scorecard-kit ledger object with a committed verdict line. Validator enforces ledger events in [8,12] here. Carries the signature rows-climb moment.
Awards TIED TO MOMENTS (Part 7 §3): each award is a stamp/seal object citing a dated moment (cross-ref the-moments), never a bare superlative.
Self-made charts (sparklines, race charts) + a stat band. Every stat named-source or confidence-tagged.

Part 7 §4 — the reader's own angle as a chapter-level element, SECOND PERSON, drawn from state (clubs, the weekly's Touchline coverage, trips, training). plan.personalisation.chapter_id must point at this chapter with state_evidence.
THE KILLER FEATURE (Part 7 §3): what actually changes next season — rules, promoted sides, transfers windows, dates — as cheat-sheet furniture, forward-committed.
Short closing beat before the colophon.

killer_features.desc: Season Review ships The Scorecards (Part 7 §3) — a plan without a scorecards chapter is invalid.
The Scorecards is 8-12 scorecard objects, planned as ledger events.
The forward-looking what-changes-next chapter is mandatory (Part 7 §3).
